item.title: SCP Draft: The Place I Belong: Re: SCP Draft: The Place I Belong
item.content:encoded:
Hey, Grig! I'll take a look for ya!

Just know that my clinical tone is meh, but I'm a lot better with dialogue.

Alrighty.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Disinformation campaigns are to be spearheaded to label SCP-XXXX-A as a UNESCO World Friendship and Peace Village to draw in more tourism.

The fact that a ConProc demands more attention is already weird enough to draw me in.
I dig it.

SCP-XXXX is a series of anomalous dreams that can occur in a certain segment of the population of Europe and Asia: most often creatives and individuals who attest to feeling at odds with society.

I feel personally called out here and I'm not sure how to mentally process this.

I just finished the Description and I don't really have any qualms with it. The dream sequences reminds me heavily of the River Styx and Charon, something I'm not sure if you did on purpose or not.
Either way, no clinical issues so far.

Aside from this:

genius loci

Did you mean 'genus'?

A little confused on that bit. I had to Google 'loci' and it gave me stuff about genetics and mathematics, neither of which this piece seems to be going for. I…actually no clue what this bit is supposed to show.

I'm normally not a fan of free verse (that is what that poetry style is, right?), but the poem written by Tefvik is wonderfully done and the allusions to the hooded figure in the SCP-XXXX dreams is also nicely done.

Especially 'blessed be the stones of your dreaming streets.'

prototypical oneirosensory visualization recording device.

Ironic…we're both currently drafting something that headcanons pioneering dream-recording Foundation tech.

I…don't know how to process this either.

I do think this is great headcanon, and I think your method of wording this is a lot better and a lot more developed than mine.

Dr. Rossi has confirmed that she is experiencing SCP-XXXX events and has been periodically for the previous three weeks.

We can clean this up and shorten it into, 'Dr. Rossi has confirmed that she has been periodically experiencing SCP-XXXX events for the previous three weeks.'

[ Initial view is of a mist shrouded body of water, which appears to be a river. The night is dark, with only a crescent moon serving as illumination.]

Unnecessary extra space before 'Initial' and after the bracket.

[The boat has stopped directly in front of subject in a manner inconsistent with the flowing water of the river, as if being held in place. The figure extends his arm out with an open palm.]

I love dream logic. This is a lovely detail to show how unearthly this place is. Other than, you know, the weird hooded figure, the mist and—
You know what I mean.

Sixteen minutes of footage are lost due to technical failure.

Both of our headcanoned dream-recording technology also involves significant lapses in dream recording to simulate the feeling of actual dream timeline-logic.

That's…frighteningly coincidental.

I love it. Love it, love it, love it <3

[Subject is within the village, walking down its streets. The stone buildings resemble architecture from the 18the century

There's an extra 'e' in '18th'

Rossi: The air is chilly, like an early spring night but not so cold as to be uncomfortable. Significant moisture in the air, consistent with misty conditions. The river in front of me is jet black, I cannot tell how deep it is by eye. I –”

This is very prose-y instead of diaogue-y (if that makes sense), but this is a dream and we could say she is trying to ground herself in a world where normal logic doesn't function.

[Sounds of a scuffle and Rossi cursing loudly cursing.]

Two 'cursing's here.

Removing either would fix it, funny enough.

Many instances8 of SCP-XXXX-1 are seen lining the square and staring at subject.]

There has been no mention of SCP-XXXX-1 up until this point, so I don't know what they're supposed to be.

Subject stands in a town square, the cobble stones shifting beneath her feet.

I absolutely adore the usage of dream logic and dream visuals here.

Answers don’t come in dreams at least not for you.

Comma after 'dreams'. Unless you're going for a sort of mysterious thing where the run on sentences show how unearthly this being is.

Also, odd how its dialogue switches to a different, bolded and italcized style here wheras earlier, it spoke like this.

Also, earlier, it was addressed as Unknown, whereas here, there's no addressing as such.

Maybe I'm just a stickler for consistency, I don't know, but I found this a tad jarring.

Wrong

No period.

Rossi: What are you talking about?

I personally imagine this character responding with 'What you do mean 'wrong?'' as a way to sass it. Can't explain why.

I just finished the first Addendum.

Hmmm…so far, I find the dialogue pretty decent. There's a good sense of mystery and a good sense of buildup, but I don't feel attached to Rossi. She feels like she's just there.

Also, the hooded figure feels a little too 'generic mysterious dream person' to me.

Like, I really dig it all, but it's missing a little bit of that pizzazz which makes me go from nodding my head and approving to making the following face:

:o

And losing all breath at the insane BS occuring before me.

Descriptions are lovely, though and the use of dream logic is very good. A little too downplayed, though, in my opinion; it's a dream and yet, despite lapses in timeline and everything being misty and hard to make out with shadowy figures, it doesn't get weird enough in my opinion. The weirdest we see is the dream figure levitating and twirling in the air. It's a dream and I think the surreal nature can be cranked up a notch or 12.

Then again, I can see that that isn't what you're really going for, so this part can be taken however you wish.

Personally, I just love seeing dream logic become as surreal and weird as possible. Probably just me.

11. There is no body of water within twenty kilometers of Kayaköy.

I like this touch here to show the difference between the 'real' version and the dream version.

Waltham: I can get to the edge of town, it’s not infinite… but then I’ll blank and it will fold in on itself; fall apart until it reforms and I’m sent right back to the fucking church..

Lovely dream logic. Sorry I'm being a broken record, I just really love weird things.

Waltham: I’m not alone here. I thought I was, but I’m not. There’s something here. I haven’t seen anything but… I’m being watched.

This feels a tad too rehearsed.

Waltham: I'll be the judge of that. I said, come out where I can see you.

You are looking right at me. Do you like it?

Needs a space between the two.

The street and buildings are also exhibiting non-Euclidean geometrics as they fold in upon themselves, shifting the camera between different elevations and rapidly restructuring from one layout to another.

This. I personally would like more stuff like this. That said, I'm having a difficult time imagining all of this. Then again, describing non-euclidean geometry is very difficult, so I'm not really sure what else to offer here.

Personally, this makes me think of the video game Control when I imagine the walls moving. Same with the streets.

Do you like it this way?

[Waltham does not respond. She is believed to be unconscious.]

Oh.

So the thing has a clumsy side. I…don't really like this scene. To me, this moment feels almost Tom and Jerry-ish in a piece that's meant to feel melancholy and strange.

And there’s no one else… You have to stay!

This was the twist that gave me chills.

After her debriefing, the current Special Containment Procedures were put in place. To date, no further SCP-XXXX events have occurred.

Well, shit. The hooded figure is just lonely and wants company. Well, that's a twist I wasn't expecting.

Other than that last bit, a good bit of the scenes just felt really rehearsed. The sequence of events were intriguing enough to keep me going and it was built up well and the dialogue was serviceable, but I think I can just summarize it as that:serviceable.

The twist? Fantastic.

I can understand the clumsy moment earlier now. The child-like clinginess and that clumsy moment from earlier, the way it begs for people to stay. It's like a lonely little kid that just wants friends.

That's a great twist.

I just think the journey along the way needs to be patched up.

Rossi and Waltham just feel like vehicles to show some weird stuff happenng.

I get the feeling that Rossi is meant to be sassy and strongwilled while Waltham is supposed to be serious and soldier-tough with a soft side, but if that's what you were going for, it doesn't come through enough.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day, Grig!

<3

If you got any questions or I was clumsy and was unclear on a few things, feel free to PM or .tell me!

item.title: Draft critiquing needed: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback. In addition, do not ever post the full text of a draft in the forums: if you wish to share a draft for feedback in future, make a sandbox page here: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/ and then share a link to it.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

item.title: Unconventional Reverse Time Capsule (Second Tab): Re: Unconventional Reverse Time Capsule (Second Tab)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I think my biggest issue with this is it just feels…very passive? Cos of the framing of like all the important stuff being passed back from the future as notes, there's not really a sense of like…the Foundation actively doing anything here; and the one time it seems like they do, they quickly give up and go back to twiddling their thumbs and it just feels…uninteresting.

In particular, tying this into a generic big spooky scp and using that as the sole source of conflict here feels really underwhelming, just because there's inherently a big deal of remoteness from this danger: like, it's in the future, it's unclear if it'll happen, the actual stakes if it does happen are unclear. Like you mention it's "Not world ending. World reshaping. A world reshaping anomaly." but there's not really any like indication of what this means?

I think for this to work, it needs more sort of…flicking from past to future: like, develop the prometheus labs stuff at the start less cos it's not very relevant, just have this be recovered from a raid and then you don't have to worry about questions like 'why does it take over a year for the foundation to grab this thing' and stuff. And then like…instead of dumping all the future notes at once, have them separated: have the current foundation do things after receiving them, and have the future notes refer to things the foundation has already done/put in motion and their effect and like…build the threat that way: have this like iterative design where they start on a shitty containment cell, the big thing breaks out and progressively it gets better and better until it works or something, y'know? Like, really allude to the notes from the future and the actions here changing the future; or alternatively…really lean into the idea that nothing we do now is helping, y'know?

Either way: the stuff from the future and the actions now should occur alternately and both should reflect each other.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

with gamma resistant walls.

do you mean 'gamma radiation'?

All personnel stationed in site wing 4B are to be issued with full hazmat gear and provided with Geiger counters and standard light-level armament.

Where is 'site wing 4B' in relation to the 'underground bunker' the SCP is stored within?

My concern here is that it makes it sound like the containment procedures aren't very effective and that in turn raises the question of why more like radiation shielding wasn't added

SCP-XXXX is a female Balaeniceps Rex typical of its species.

I'd probably add a footnote here to indicate what a Balaeniceps Rex is

SCP-XXXX's beak contains a microchip of unknown origin that produces large amounts of gamma radiation through a currently unknown process hereafter classified as a Class-A incident.

This is a really janky sentence because up to the 'hereafter' implies 'this is a continuous, ongoing thing', whereas designating it as a Class-A incident indicates 'this is a sporadic event' and it needs cleaned up to so it indicates like…how often this process happens

SCP-XXXX will regurgitate between one and four instances of SCP-XXXX-1.

You have to define -1 before using the designation: saying it regurgitates between one and four inanimate objects of unknown origin would be more effective so we have some idea of what that is.

most often anomalous pieces of technology and components of machinery, many of which are compatible with items in Prometheus Labs confiscation vaults 1A, 36G, 45I and 47█.

Generally I'm not a fan of lengthy struckthrough sections, particularly when there's not a clear idea of why they've been struckthrough at the time and particularly when they include key information that contextualises what is happening

Standard anomalous item recovery and radiation safety procedure 112-G is to be enacted after SCP-XXXX's microchip ceases radioactivity.

This is something which should be in the conprocs.

SCP-XXXX was recovered in 1999 during a raid on an abandoned Prometheus Labs facility in Butare, Rwanda. SCP-XXXX was found severely malnourished and injured, presumably having been trapped in the facility for several months.

This just…feels weird? Like why didn't they raid the facility for several months? Why didn't Prometheus Labs do a more thorough decommissioning?

The facility was heavily contaminated presumably due to an unrecorded number of Class-A incidents before discovery.

Contaminated with what? I don't believe gamma radiation tends to stick around long since it's y'know, high energy photons, so the room shouldn't be heavily contaminated with it unless there's a radiation source other than the SCP.

as well as a █████ brand computer drive with a set of files dedicated to logs of the facility's construction

I feel like you could rephrase to 'hard drive' to avoid having an unnecessary blackbox here.

See addendum XXXX-1 for recovered documents.

cut this. The addendum is right after this so we don't need a sentence saying 'read this for recovered documents' followed by a title saying 'recovered documents'.

They'll have my head for this, but I know the ones who will take the best care of her will be The Foundation.

this is dated to a year at least before the foundation raided this place so did this doctor like….just do the worst job of this?

Incident Timeline

This feels like a weird combination of awkwardly expository and awkwardly uninformative? Like there's a hint that at some point, something happened to cause the O5 council to sequester it away but there's not really like…enough here for us to even begin speculating on why, y'know?

The following document was produced by SCP-XXXX during a Class-A incident.

When?

The problem with this is that it feels like it needs to be contextualised based on the unknown incident in the previous log except we're given so little information that we can't tell if this is the cause of it or a result of it or both or what.

The following document is transcribed from an SD card produced by SCP-XXXX during a Class-A incident.

This document is in dire need of empty lines between the paragraphs to space it out: adding a space after the > on a line will let you put one in (or you can use "[[div class="blockquote"]]" at the start and "[[/div]]" at the end to not need to worry about having every line start with "> ")

and the foundation is authorized to attempt termination if SCP-14821 is not recontained within three hours of reaching land.

this is kinda clunky but it also completely undercuts the danger: if SCP-14821 is so dangerous, it feels like the foundation should attempt termination much sooner than this.

Under order of 05-4, the construction of site 212 has begun. However, due to lack of items or documents produced by SCP-XXXX, it has been halted until further notice.

as an ending, this is just…really anticlimactic?

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Looking for a review for Thermites: SCP Draft: Thermites
item.content:encoded:
A species of termites who are capable of collecting an manipulating metals. They form a complex society with trade, hierarchy and art.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Here it is! Got the first Greenlight in May and now its December and I finally got a first draft done.
This is my first SCP and I'm really happy with how its turned out so far.

SCP-XXXX: Thermites
Word Count: 3,823
Greenlit post: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13365263/scp-idea:thermites
Draft: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/cloudncali

Looking forward to what the community thinks.

This article started as a silly twist on the word thermite (the pyrotechnic powder) actually being Thermal Termites. The narrative developed from my fondness of SCPs with more human elements. The SCP Foundation is full of people from different backgrounds, its always fun to see different personalities show through the cold and stiff atmosphere of the foundation.

Edit: Massive rework of grammar and prose. Should be easier to read now.
